source.label: The structure-function condition for a shifted finite configuration

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: For a nonempty finite multiset of complex points rho = beta + i gamma with polynomial F and real h: |F(h+s)| > |F(h+1-conj(s))| for all Re s > 1/2 iff every beta <= 1/2 + h and some beta < 1/2 + h. The proof is the identity |h+s-rho|^2 - |h+1-conj(s)-rho|^2 = (2 sigma - 1)(2h + 1 - 2 beta).
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof. The same identity is the step in Lagarias's Lemma 2.1 (arXiv math/0601653), so on that source's product formula the de Branges structure-function condition for xi(1/2 + h - iz) holds exactly when xi has no zero with real part above 1/2 + h; unconditional for h >= 1/2, and never for h <= 0. Shows the Hermite-Biehler lead's defining inequality on the whole half-plane is the zero-free statement at each positive shift; at a single point it is weaker. Inner-product conditions on the associated space are not examined.
claims.rationale: Shows that the modulus inequality at a fixed positive shift is the zero-free statement; the lead stays open on the consequence side (zeros of the sum functions) and the inner-product conditions.
claims.next_action: Quantify the count of off-line zeros of the sum function for a finite configuration with k points right of the shifted line, and decide the converse.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry; the xi version rests on a read source's product formula.
notes.significance: Context: elementary; a small sharpening of a published lemma's statement. Novelty not claimed.
notes.relationships: Companion of the logarithmic derivative sign criteria; both are forms of the zero-free statement.

relationships: The half-plane sign criterion is the infinitesimal form of the same modulus inequality.
As a hypothesis it would extend the unconditional range of shifts from h >= 1/2 to h >= 3/8; not used.
